newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt minister says militants call for truce a ruse.
newsitem.headline: Egypt minister says militants call for truce a ruse.

text.p: Egyptian Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi said on Sunday a call for a ceasefire by jailed members of the biggest Moslem militant group fighting to overthrow the state was a ruse intended to improve their public image.
Earlier this month, six imprisoned leaders of the militant al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) issued a statement calling on their followers to stop unilaterally all violent acts.

The appeal, read out by an alleged militant at a trial earlier this month and repeated on Saturday, was rejected by exiled Gama'a leaders who said they would continue their armed struggle to transform Egypt into a strict Moslem state.

"These groups felt the people were against them and they are trying to win over public opinion by calling for this ceasefire. They want to make the people sympathetic to their activities that contravene Islam. This is a manoeuvre," Alfi told reporters during the graduation ceremony of police academy students.
More than 1,000 people have been killed since the group took up arms against the government in 1992.

Police say they have broken the back of the military wing of the Gama'a through crackdowns and the number of attacks has declined sharply since the mid-1990s, when the militants were killing about one policeman a day.

Yasser al-Sirri, an exiled Islamist who has been sentenced to death in Egypt, said the ceasefire did not show there was a rift in the group. "That (truce) statement is their independent reasoning, but it does not change the core of the cause...this regime is illegal and does not respect human rights."
